messenger_reliability.builder_why: The scroll is better and it is not fixed, and the diagnosis I gave for it was incomplete. `Written` wrapped its text in `Inked`, a ShaderMask, so every note's subtree needed a compositing layer and its tear had to be composed as an image rather than drawn. That is gone: the capture report carries `SlicedMasks.composed` now and it reads 1 on Pulse, 0 on Us, 11 for a whole screenful of Chat, 6 on 07 and 1 on 06 — where the old behaviour was one bake per note as the thread scrolled. And the scroll's build cost fell by twelve per cent: 179 frames of 775 over 400 ms at p95 782, against 203 of 793 at p95 897. Twelve per cent is not what removing a bake per note should look like, so the baking was not the whole cost and I do not yet know what the rest is. So I put the counter on the scroll — 11 had no `report` step at all, so the one number this claim rests on was recorded for every scene except the one that scrolls — and re-shot it. **Twelve masks, across a fling through 8,075 rows in seven throws.** The baking is gone and the spikes are not the baking: 179 frames still cost more than 400 ms to build, in the same bimodal shape, 4 ms or about 780 with nothing between. Three cycles of this row have rested on a diagnosis that its own instrument has now disproved, and the fix was still worth making — it removed a real cost — but it was not the cost. The next hypothesis, named so it can be killed as cleanly: the hand fonts carry contextual alternates and every new note shapes a paragraph through them, which is on the build thread. Build with `fontFeatures` empty, scroll the same anchor, read the same number. I have not done it and I am not claiming it. The rest of the row moved. A refused message carries `send it again` in the margin beside the refusal, where the timestamp is, instead of only inside a long-press menu — which is exactly where a reader was told, on the artifact named for the messenger's states, that there was nothing. `states_on_the_glass` counts only rows that are wholly in the frame, and anything clipped is listed separately with how much of it is showing: 13 claimed a read mark for a row that was 125 device pixels of blank paper with its ink above the top edge, and there was no read mark anywhere in the picture. A photograph hit in search carries its print, where three rows read 'you sent a photograph — Eight in the morning.' with nothing to tell them apart. An undeveloped print is photographic stock rather than eight per cent of black over the card behind it, and the Moments record counts how many tiles are still waiting for one. In 08 the message that crosses is opened, where it sat for eighty-six frames as a blank torn sheet with the reader's name on the outside. And a console line that says a request failed now says which request, with its status and method and URL. 13 carries the typing indicator and four of the five delivery states in one frame: sent three times, 'it would not go' in red, and **going** — the in-flight state, which has not appeared in any capture before. `queued` and `read` are not in this one, and I would rather say which than imply all five: the row that was read has scrolled above the anchor, and the dropped requests meant to leave a row sitting in the outbox let it through. 13 was shot three times, and what the shots taught is worth more than the picture. The first shot came back with all five rows reading 'going' and no typing indicator, because the latency a slow send injects is on every request rather than on the message that asked for it, so nothing else could settle and the far phone's own typing frame could not cross inside the window the step waits in. The staging resets the wire now. The second came back with the indicator dark while its own log said `awaited: partner_typing, got: true` — eleven seconds passed between the frame arriving and the shutter opening, against an indicator that lapses after six, because a slow send, a wait, a three-second scroll and a two-second shutter all sat between them. The thread is pinned to the end before anything is timed now and only the send and the shutter are inside the lapse. The record and the picture disagreed because the harness is slow, not because the app is wrong, and that is worth writing down because it is the second time this cycle a fault in the framing read as a fault in the build. MANIFEST.json records when each artifact was written, so the set says which were re-shot. Still against this row: no second device anywhere; transport local on every reliability run with the tailnet pending; and a first launch that imports the year still costs seconds.

material_truth.builder_why: The paper-shaped feeling objects have a surface, and it was two faults rather than one. The material's grain is written in UV cycles and an object's UV spans its own width, so a sheet's 120-cycle mottle — a feature every 1.75 mm across 210 mm of paper — became a feature every third of a millimetre on a 40 mm card, with a relief a fourteenth of one, which is under a pixel at any density an object renders at. That is written in millimetres and converted now. And a mesh built from explicit vertices has no UV layer at all, so the Texture Coordinate node's UV output is (0,0) over the whole surface and the material resolves to one flat colour whatever is in it — every object folded out of raw polygons was in that state, which is why the crane measured 0.49 grey levels of local standard deviation against 9.0 for a paper stock and why four critics read these as untextured low-poly renders. They were, for want of anywhere to put the tooth. Measured on the packed WebP the app actually loads, 40 px windows of an object's own interior: 25 objects, median 5.03, flattest 2.22, where obj_dog_ear packed at 0.89. The desk has pores in it. Five renders to work out that the number I had chosen to chase was the wrong one: the anisotropy went 5.76, 5.16, 5.60, 5.11, 5.13 while the surface went from painted stripes to visible oak, because a pore adds to the gradient across the grain as much as along it. What moved is the fine detail — the share of spectral power above 35 per cent of Nyquist, which is the measure the material critic used — 1.23 per cent before and 1.83 now on the day desk, 2.20 on the dusk one. The pores were seven per cent below the wood round them, which is a smudge; a vessel cut open by a saw is twenty to thirty-five per cent down. I also said in a commit that the denoiser was averaging them away and that is not established: turning it off and quadrupling the samples moved the fine detail from 1.12 to 1.16 per cent, which is nothing. It stays off because a surface whose detail is the same size as its noise should not be denoised, but the reason they were invisible was that they were too pale. What is still flat, and now has an instrument: tools/check/flat.py looks for a pale, paper-coloured 80 px window flatter than real paper, and it reads six of ten stills clean — 01_pulse 2.40 where it was 0.72, 12_search 3.17 where it was 1.78 — and four not: 03_us with twenty windows under the floor, 05_settings with thirty-two, 17_setup_pwa with twenty, 14_media_viewer with thirteen. That is a different fault from the objects and I have not fixed it: those are the big pale slabs, where a stock rendered at a large size has its tooth spread under the eye. The check ships the numbers rather than my word for them. And the letters still repeat: one mark in six has a twin at IoU 0.80.

emotional_transmission.builder_why: A state reaches a phone after it is shut. logs/reception.json records four arrivals at the service worker and the fourth is `state_declared` — 'said how they are' — drawn quietly, which is the treatment the registry gives it, so what the picture shows is the worker deciding not to interrupt. Every record it had ever held was a feeling or a message, and a state crossing to a closed phone is this row's own subject. The vocabulary is separable by a finger now, and the check that said it already was has been replaced. It compared exact strings and outlines in normalised time, neither of which is what a hand does: an emotional critic pointed at stuck with me, eight pulses at a flat 220 over 480 ms, against overwhelmed, ten pulses at a mean 227.5 over 500 — four per cent of duration and three of amplitude apart, and the check called them distinct because their strings differ. haptics.py measures forty-millisecond bins of real time with amplitude to the power 0.6, plus a term for the difference in length, because a single thirty-millisecond tap and a five-hundred-millisecond three-part snap are not the same event and score close on bins alone. The closest pair was 20.3 against a median of 59; four waveforms are reshaped and the closest pair is 21.1 with nothing under the floor. breathe's pattern now matches the sound that was composed for it — the one sound of thirty-six whose length disagreed with its own waveform. The corner that reaches the whole layer was 35 per cent of its box at rest: twenty-six logical pixels, 3.5 grey levels against the sheet, and invisible over the viewer's dark ground at 93.3 inside its own footprint against 96.0 outside. Half the box now, with a lit edge inside the crease, because a real fold has one side in the light and that is what gives it an edge on paper and over a photograph both. And reliability.json certifies a feeling and a state crossing the wire — squeeze arriving at intensity 0.62, the number it was sent at, because an intensity that does not survive the wire is a feeling that arrives as a different feeling. Nineteen capabilities were all messenger paths; there are twenty-one and two of them are this row's. What stands: no artifact in this set was made by a device that can vibrate — channel_here is 'page' for every capture — so the row's own test, a feeling identifiable by its pattern with the screen face down, cannot be run on anything here.

coherence.builder_why: An open line off the list is an empty box wherever it is drawn. The Us desk led one with a cross while the same kind of item in the thread carried a box — the same event marked two ways in one build, and the desk's way said the opposite of what it meant, because a cross through a line is how anyone strikes one off. Two documents said more than the build does, and now say what it does. docs/EVENT_TYPES.md promised treatments that branch on what happened — quiet for a date planned, interruptive for one scheduled — while the registry is Notify.quiet flat and nothing keys on the payload. It also cannot be, on the path that matters: a push carries the kind and the sender and nothing else, on purpose, so a treatment depending on the action would have to put the action in the push. And tools/lint/strings.py reported `strings_read: 116` with no denominator, which reads as coverage; it reads 116 of 3,668 literals in lib/, three per cent, and says so and says what it cannot see. DIFF.json says that --rotate overwrites the baseline it has just measured against, and every row carries the hash and the write time of the file it was compared with, so a number in it can still be attributed after the rotation — a completeness pass found all fifteen baseline files byte-identical to the capture that shipped beside them and was right to call that unreproducible. BRIEFING.md now states the rule that folds the code reading into this row as the lower of the two, says what `blocking` is for — forty-three findings and not one marked blocking while three rows failed their floors — and points at evidence/scenes/, which is the recipe a reader needs to tell a fault in the app from a fault in the framing. Two structural rules that could not fail now can. The storage-driver rule missed a conditional import, which is exactly how this codebase reaches a platform's driver and exactly the form it could not see; and the tailnet cold start wrote a `pending` file and returned before any expect(), so the runner counted it as one more passing line. It reports as skipped. What is still open and I have not touched it: the Moments lens labels are stamped on the wood while the chips twenty pixels below them sit on paper. Converting them moves the band the gallery is framed against and I was not willing to move an artifact's framing hours before the capture that has to show everything else.

anti_goal.builder_why: The finding I marked myself down two points for last cycle is closed at the source. Every paper-shaped feeling object now has a surface — 25 objects on the packed WebP the app loads, median 5.03 local standard deviation, flattest 2.22, where seven were under 1.1 and the flattest read 0.42 — and the desk has pores in it, 1.83 per cent of spectral power above 35 per cent of Nyquist against 1.23. A pale card with a drop shadow under it is the brief's own words for a failure of the whole visual concept, and that is what those objects were. There are still no badges, no points, no streak warnings and no guilt in any string; the app never names itself and never addresses a user. What holds this row under full marks is what held it before and what tools/check/flat.py now measures: four stills still carry pale slabs flatter than real paper — 05_settings has thirty-two windows under the floor — and until a reader can look at every surface in the set and see a photograph rather than an approximation, this row is not a ten. It is better than the eight I gave it last cycle because the objects were the worst of it and they are fixed; it is not a nine yet because the slabs are the same fault in a different place and I have only instrumented them.

declined.finding: Five module cards are machine-cut to 0.00-0.79 px rms on all four edges (03_us.png)
declined.reason: Declined on the merits. Those pieces are index cards, and an index card is machine-cut; the critic says so themselves and notes the anti-goal is not tripped because the stock is a real scan. Making a guillotined edge wobble would be less true, not more. What is worth doing and is not done is a cut-edge mask that gives the edge a lit face, so it reads as a card seen from slightly above rather than as a rectangle.

declined.finding: The three Moments lens labels are stamped on the wood while the person and range chips twenty pixels below them sit on paper (04_moments.png)
declined.reason: Agreed and not done. The lenses are a facet selector like the search's, and the search's are chips on paper, so paper is the coherent answer. Converting them changes the height of the band the gallery is framed against, and I was not willing to move the framing of an artifact hours before the capture that has to show everything else this cycle fixed. It is the first thing in the next one.
